questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One of the important aspects for choosing Bologna as an exchange destination was that it had a great student life and good university vibes. It is a really nice city with a lot of students and student life in general in Bologna is really great.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My overall experience in Bologna was really great, it is a lovely city and general student life in the city is really good. The downside is that housing is quite expensive due to high demand and it can be a bit difficult to find a room. Furthermore, if you are on your bachelors (at least in economics) the amount of courses (in my experience) provided in english was a little limited.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When I arrived in Italy it was a little bit difficult to find information and coordinate with the university regarding courses, attendance etc. But in the end it all worked out. The Italians are generally not as organized and fixed on deadlines and formality regarding course registration etc. as i'm used to in Denmark. But in the end it all works out, but patience can be important in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You can go to the student desk, but in general it was a bit difficult to find information in the beginning, however it all worked out fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: In the beginning it was difficult to find information on courses etc., and the system for registration at the university was way too crowded so it took some time before I even officially got registered at my courses. But again everything worked out, and once your registered the UNIBO app is very good for information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. The housing situation in Bologna is very chaotic. There is not a lot of available rooms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive, but I had a good experience. The city is very walkable no matter where you live, you are always close to everything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Expensive and very high demand on rooms, so very difficult to find a room.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Mentioned earlier.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to register for your courses online and do a online check in at the University before you were originally registered. The problem was that check in was only open a few days a week at specific hours and it was very difficult to get through due to high demand / server problems. It seemed like they did not have the capacity to register everybody in the beginning. So the first weeks was a bit chaotic because of this I think.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write professors of your courses and they were quite good at responding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fine

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it chill. The registration process can be a bit frustrating if your used to very organized systems, but it will work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The acedemic programmes was quite decent, but some of them could have been a bit better.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Course level was a little bit easier compared to what I am used to, but when you are on exchange it is quite nice. Also I think it depends on what courses you take, I also had one course which was quite difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More lecture focused, where I am more used to exercise classes, which i prefer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public Finance and Public Policy, Corporate Finance, Introduction to Behavioral Economics, Industrial Organization.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Behavioral Economics and Industrial Organization were very interesting courses and well organized.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student life was very nice. In general there is a lot of opportunities to enjoy life in Bologna, however I would say there could have been more organised sports, clubs etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not attend anything "through" the university but arranged stuff by my self with other exchange students. Trips, football, padel tennis, food, drinks etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat and enjoy the good Italian food. Go out on bars and enjoy the cheap espresso and approach the Italian lifestyle with siesta and aperitif

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a lot of trips around Italy. Bologna is very well connected with a lot of cities around Italy. You can easily go to a lot of the Italian cities in North Italy like Verona, Venedig, Lake Como, Lake Garda, Firenze, Rome. Go visit some nature, a vineyard and maybe the dolomites. Take a trip to South Italy which is easily accecable with the train to Napoli which only take 3,5 hours.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, the Italian culture is easy to adjust to and they speak english very well in Bologna, also there is a lot of other exchange students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out and enjoy the city, you will find a lot of other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The more laidback lifestyle, siesta, coffee and aperitif. Going out to eat way more often etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about the practical paperwork etc. it will work out. Go and enjoy the city and think about the courses you take.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of really nice people. Getting 3 months more of summer. Learning (some) Italian. Getting to travel around Italy a lot and eat a lot of good food.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: NO

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
